principles: Single source of truth: define the category-to-blocking-decision table ONCE in core and consume from every gate
No silent passes: every category-allowed path emits a structured audit event into process-events.jsonl

Conservative direction of change: only the 3 explicitly-handled categories (koala_metadata / runtime_artifact / declared_artifact) get a pass; everything else (including unknown future categories) stays blocking by default
drivers: B-c9f5 REVIEW/TEST loops still recur on non-material dirt because the existing gates ignore B-6326 classifier output for the blocking decision
Without this story, B-3506 auto-commit and B-cf60 artifact declarations do not actually unblock the gates — they only relabel categories
Future audit needs to prove that gate decisions were not coincidence: a structured audit log makes silent loosening detectable in regression and post-mortem

options.name: A: Core dirty-gate-policy table + consume from story-advance + validation-executor + audit log
pros: Single source of truth in core/dirty-gate-policy.ts
Both gates call the same evaluator — divergence impossible by construction
Audit log surfaces every allowed pass for post-mortem
Easy to extend: adding a new category requires touching the policy table only
Allowlist (not blocklist) semantics: unknown future categories default to blocking
cons: Touches 2 gate consumer files and adds 1 new core file — 3 touchpoints

options.name: B: Inline the category check at each consumer (no shared table)
pros: Smallest diff: just an if-check in story-advance.ts and validation-executor.ts
cons: Two divergent decision points — exactly the trap B-c9f5 incident shape created
Future category additions require touching every consumer

options.name: C: Move the policy into config.ts as a static map
cons: config.ts already has too many responsibilities
Audit log has no natural home there
Validation-protocol-smoke would need to reach into config to assert policy — coupling test surface to config schema

chosen: A: Core dirty-gate-policy table + consume from story-advance + validation-executor + audit log
rationale: Choose A because the reported risk (silent divergence between gate consumers) is exactly the B-c9f5 incident shape, and option B re-creates that shape directly. C keeps SOT but commingles policy with config which violates Data/Machine/Fn separation and complicates testing. A places the policy as pure data + pure decision fn in core/dirty-gate-policy.ts, consumed by story-advance.ts (TEST pre-check + DONE gate row) and validation-executor.ts (side-effect guard). Each consumer also writes a structured audit event to process-events.jsonl when >=1 path is allowed to pass, so post-mortem and regression can prove that the loosening was intentional. Allowlist-direction (only 3 categories pass; everything else including future categories blocks) keeps the safety bound that B-c9f5 demanded.

preMortem.scenario: Future category added to DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES silently passes because someone forgets to update the policy table
preMortem.trigger: A new value e.g. snapshot_artifact_changes is added to the enum but the policy table still uses an allowlist that does not enumerate it
preMortem.consequence: Material regression hidden in the new category passes both TEST gate and DONE gate; team only notices when production breaks
preMortem.mitigation: Policy table uses an exhaustive switch + ts-pattern-style runtime assertion: every DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES entry MUST appear in the table or the evaluator throws. Smoke test enumerates DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES.length === table.entries.length and fails when out of sync.

preMortem.scenario: Audit log is silently dropped because process-events.jsonl write fails
preMortem.trigger: Disk full / permission error during append; current write paths swallow errors
preMortem.consequence: Policy lets a path pass, but no audit record exists — silent loosening cannot be reconstructed in post-mortem
preMortem.mitigation: Audit-writer must (1) throw on write failure to abort the gate decision, OR (2) return a fallback warning row attached to the gate output so the user sees AUDIT WRITE FAILED. Default to (1): no audit, no pass. Smoke test simulates fs failure and asserts gate falls back to blocking.

preMortem.scenario: Policy gets imported by validation-executor but not by story-advance, or vice versa
preMortem.trigger: Refactor accidentally removes import in one consumer; existing hardcoded if(dirty>0) fail path remains as dead code
preMortem.consequence: One gate uses category policy, the other uses any-dirty-blocks — divergent behavior, B-c9f5 incident shape returns
preMortem.mitigation: Both consumers MUST call evaluateDirtyGate(classification) from the shared module — no inline category checks allowed. Smoke test fails if any consumer file mentions DIRTY_WORKTREE_CATEGORIES outside of importing the policy module (grep-based assertion in flow-stability-smoke).
